title: Chicken and broccoli stir-fry

items: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
3 cups broccoli florets (from 1 medium head), bite-size
2 medium carrots, peeled and sliced ¼ inch thick on an angle
1 cup frozen shelled edamame or peas

steps: Whisk the sauce ingredients in a small bowl until the cornstarch dissolves. Pat the chicken dry and season with the salt.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the chicken in one layer and cook 5–7 min, turning once it's browned, until no pink remains and it reads 165°F. Move to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil, the broccoli and carrots. Stir-fry 2 min, until the broccoli turns bright green.
Add 2 Tbsp water and cover the pan. Steam 2 min, until the carrots are crisp-tender. Uncover, add the edamame or peas and stir-fry 1 min more.
Return the chicken and any juices. Whisk the sauce again, since the cornstarch settles, and pour it in.
Stir 1–2 min, until the sauce bubbles, thickens and coats everything in a glossy layer.
Serve over rice and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Cut the vegetables to a similar size so they cook evenly.
Thighs stay juicier than breast and are harder to overcook.
Add a pinch of red pepper flakes or 1 tsp sriracha to the sauce for heat.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water, or in the microwave, until hot (165°F). Freezes up to 2 months, though the broccoli softens.
